title: The rally broadens, but capital is still expensive

summary.changed: Broad Black Friday recovery, with chips outperforming Nvidia.
summary.missed: Fund issuance and price gains measure different things.
summary.watch: Oil supply, yields and normal-volume trading.

sections.heading: Broad rebound, not a return to the peak
paragraphs: At the November 27 close, Portfolio Terminal and Reuters show a post-Thanksgiving rebound. S&P 500: 7,297.49 (+1.60% daily, +5.60% weekly, +7.12% trailing year); Nasdaq Composite: 24,129.50 (+2.31% daily, +6.68% weekly, +3.94% trailing year); Dow Jones: 50,774.94 (+1.18% daily, +5.46% weekly, +7.06% trailing year); Russell 2000: 2,750.30 (+1.71% daily, +6.53% weekly, +10.63% trailing year). The S&P remains 6.67% below its October 6 peak. Reuters calls this its strongest week since April 2025. The shortened session limits conclusions about persistence.

sections.heading: Chips rise without Nvidia leadership
paragraphs: Reuters reports Micron up 7.6%, Marvell 7.3% and Sandisk nearly 16%, against only 0.8% for Nvidia. Portfolio Terminal reports consumer discretionary up 1.99%, technology 1.86% and health care 0.17%. Interpretation: the rebound is not dependent on one stock, but does not establish improved orders or cash flow.

sections.heading: Macro and bonds do not confirm the rally
paragraphs: BEA's November 25 second estimate puts Q3 annualized real GDP growth at 4.3%, versus 3.4% initially and 2.2% in Q2. This is a revision surprise, not a consensus comparison. The US Treasury reports a 4.94% ten-year yield on November 27. Reuters notes expectations of a December rate increase. Growth supports earnings, but a high discount rate can constrain multiples.

sections.heading: Flows: ETFs versus mutual funds
paragraphs: ICI's November 25 estimates for the week ended November 18 show $76.73 billion ETF net issuance against $29.01 billion long-term mutual fund outflows, a combined $47.72 billion inflow. Money market assets reached $7.98 trillion on November 24. These aggregates cover different periods and do not establish that this money funded Friday's rally.

sections.heading: Oil, dollar and commodity funds
paragraphs: Reuters: Brent settled at $95.44 a barrel (down 1.2% daily, up about 3% weekly); WTI at $83.08 (down 0.7% daily). Portfolio Terminal: DXY 104.02 (+0.34%), GLD $334.40 (+2.12%), USO $137.50 (−1.71%), IBIT $33.86 (−0.62%). Fund prices are not spot prices or flows. Oil supply risk could complicate disinflation.

market_map: Friday November 27 closes; no live Saturday US quotes.
contrarian: Bull case: earnings and broad participation justify recovery. Bear case: holiday liquidity and short covering exaggerate gains while financing costs remain high. No verified positioning data establish short covering.
bottom_line: Watch cash flow and capital costs rather than extrapolating a single session.
disclaimer: No verified current consensus, individual fund flows or company-order changes; no investment recommendation.
